## tmh post

Send a POST request to any API path

### Synopsis

Sends a POST request to a path relative to the API base URL, which already ends in /v1, with the same authentication and error handling as the resource commands. Each run sends a generated Idempotency-Key, so transient failures are retried safely. A literal {orgId} in the path is replaced by the Organization your credentials are bound to.

```
tmh post <path> [flags]
```

### Examples

```
  tmh post /organizations/{orgId}/learners -d email=ana@example.com -d name="Ana Example"
  tmh post /organizations/{orgId}/webhook-subscriptions --data @subscription.json
```

### Options

```
      --content-type string   Content-Type of the body (default "application/json")
  -d, --data stringArray      body field as key=value (dotted keys nest, key[]=v appends, key:=<json> sends JSON), or the whole body as @file, @- for stdin, or a JSON document; repeatable
  -h, --help                  help for post
      --if-match string       send If-Match with this ETag, for a conditional write
      --no-auth               send no Access token, even when logged in; public operations such as /courses never get one
      --query stringArray     query parameter as key=value; repeatable
```

      --idempotency-key string   Idempotency-Key for the write, instead of a generated one

      --profile string           profile to use: "sandbox" (default) or "live"

      --verbose                  print method, path, status, latency and request id of each HTTP attempt to stderr
